f54ec608d64c.title: FHIR content
f54ec608d64c.content: TR… . On this page . | Representations, and why only one is taken | The artefact index is reconstructed | Where the rules live | . This page is generated from docs/source/fhir-fhir-content/ — each section below links to its own source. ✎ Edit QA… TR… . A FHIR Implementation Guide is a published, versioned package of profiles, terminology, examples and prose that says how FHIR is to be used for one purpose. This page describes how IG content is shaped in the graph. Two things distinguish it from the other content kinds here. It is compiled — an author writes FHIR Shorthand and a tool produces the resources, so the thing an author edits and the thing a reader fetches are different artefacts. And it is published at canonical URLs that other IGs resolve against, so its identity is a URL and a version rather than a path in a repository.

72102ff376f3.title: Representations, and why only one is taken
72102ff376f3.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The IG Publisher emits three serialisations of every resource — JSON, XML and Turtle — plus HTML per resource page. Only the JSON is taken, wrapped in JSON-LD and JSON Schema; RDF, where needed, is projected from the JSON-LD. The site neither renders nor links a resource’s XML or Turtle copy. A representation that arrives and is not taken is recorded as a refusal. The Publisher’s per-page HTML is a rendering, not a serialisation, and is not used: it has no front matter, so the navbar, language bar, QA badges and translation surface cannot reach it. IG pages are rendered as folio pages instead (see ig-render-jekyll).

3744f26cc500.title: The artefact index is reconstructed
3744f26cc500.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . No FHIR IG publishes an index of its own artefacts. Four files each carry part of one: . | view | carries | . | package.tgz → package/.index.json | filename, resourceType, id for every file | . | canonicals.json | id, type, url, version, name — canonical resources only | . | artifacts.html | the only source of an artefact’s category | . | package.manifest.json | package-level metadata | . The index is reconstructed, and each field records its source file, because coverage varies: canonicals.json covers about a tenth of one published IG’s artefacts and all of another’s. Two files look like indexes and are not: . | ValueSets.schema.json at the published root is a schema, not an index. It describes an enumeration endpoint’s response and carries an example that holds the list. | openapi/openapi.json is not the IG’s API sidecar set. In at least one published IG it is an unrelated domain API, so an ingest that globs for OpenAPI-shaped files mis-files it. | .

c07dedd9aa66.title: The FHIR IG Publisher
c07dedd9aa66.content: TR… . On this page . | What one run emits | What only it can do | What it cannot tell you | The version is not pinned | Where the rules live | . This page is generated from docs/source/fhir-ig-publisher/ — each section below links to its own source. ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The FHIR IG Publisher is HL7’s tool that turns an implementation guide’s sources into a published site. Here it is a mechanical actor: a process step with declared inputs and outputs. In a build with pre- and post-processing it is one step among many. API sidecars, JSON Schemas and JSON-LD vocabularies on a published IG are written by scripts after it exits, not by the Publisher.

bca9308ccebe.title: What one run emits
bca9308ccebe.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . | output | notes | . | output/ | the rendered site: HTML per resource and per page (input/pagecontent/, sushi-config.yaml pages:) | . | {ResourceType}-{id}.json | the structured surface everything downstream reads | . | .xml, .ttl | the same resource in two more serialisations; this platform reads only the JSON | . | package.tgz → package/.index.json | filename, resourceType, id (index version 2) | . | canonicals.json, package.manifest.json | partial views of the artefact set | . | artifacts.html | the only source of an artefact’s category | . | qa.json | the validation record | . | POT files | translatable strings | . The list changes between releases and the version is not pinned (below), so any count needs a date and a version. It emits no artefact index. ValueSets.schema.json is a schema whose example happens to hold a list; it is not an index. An index must be reconstructed from the four partial views above, and provenance records all four because which one matters differs per IG.

8730585070fe.title: What only it can do
8730585070fe.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . | Profile validation: every resource against its profiles and FHIR version. | Dependency-closure resolution with version pinning (for a clinical guideline IG: hl7.terminology, hl7.fhir.uv.extensions.r4, hl7.fhir.uv.cql, hl7.fhir.uv.cpg, hl7.fhir.uv.crmi, hl7.fhir.uv.sdc). | Terminology expansion against a terminology server. | . None can be recomputed from its output, so a cached build is a cache: its indices, dependency edges and versions were true when it was written. Expansion fails quietly. Against a dead or restricted terminology server there are fewer expansions and the consuming steps warn and continue. A thin vocabulary is not evidence of a thin ValueSet; check that expansion ran.

297721951f6b.title: What it cannot tell you
297721951f6b.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Its metadata exports, measured on two IGs: . | export | trust IG | immunizations IG | . | valueset-ref-list.json ValueSet→CodeSystem edges | 17 over 14 | 431 over 252 | . | codesystem-ref-list.json uses populated | 0 of 15 | 0 of 14 | . | usage-stats.json extension→path | 6 | 35 (+5 profiles) | . | uses is declared but never populated, so “no dependencies” and “not computed” look the same. | No dependencies among Library, PlanDefinition or Measure. In the immunizations IG that is 279 + 138 + 41 artefacts, about 61 %: the CQL and decision logic. | . The exports reach terminology, not logic. Logic dependencies need an AST emitted by the tool itself, which means changing org.hl7.fhir.core, not only the Publisher. Re-measure before quoting: a release can close either gap.

135b2d73fac7.title: The version is not pinned
135b2d73fac7.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . A common build fetches the latest publisher.jar on every run: . - name: Update the image to the latest publisher uses: docker://hl7fhir/ig-publisher-base:latest with: args: curl -L https://github.com/HL7/fhir-ig-publisher/releases/latest/download/publisher.jar … . Two builds of the same commit can differ, and the output does not say which version made it, so “the build changed” cannot be told from “the content changed”. A cached AST must therefore record its toolchain (Publisher, core and SUSHI versions) as a required field.

2eb71e38a983.title: fhir-harness
2eb71e38a983.content: The bare FHIR IG pipeline. SUSHI compiles FHIR Shorthand, the IG Publisher builds and validates the guide, and the result is assembled and published to a pages branch. There is no pre-processing and no post-processing, so any FHIR implementation guide can use this layer. input/fsh/ → SUSHI → fsh-generated/resources/ input/pagecontent/ ┐ sushi-config.yaml ┘ → IG Publisher (JVM, Docker) → output/ → pages branch .

e331ab9dec61.title: Where it sits
e331ab9dec61.content: It sits on the content core and may import from it. The layers that build particular guides sit on top of this one and pass their own names in as configuration. This layer never names them.

39b07fece2cf.title: Covers
39b07fece2cf.content: The ig-ast kind viewer, declared by this layer, for every ig-ast directory an instance in the checkout declares. Drawn by this layer’s Tool ig-ast-pages (scripts/gen-ig-ast-pages.ts): a hub at <locale>/fhir-harness/ig-ast/ and one page per declaring instance under it. The route key is the one index.json records for this wireframe. How this was drawn . From the pages gen-ig-ast-pages --site writes in a checkout of the index, not from a built site. Only one instance, an IG layer above this one, declares an ig-ast directory, and its branch family is not restored in a checkout, so the drawing is the hub and the “unknown” instance page. That instance is drawn as <ig>: this layer names no layer above it. It is kept beside the viewer it draws: check:wireframes reads the wireframes/ of every declared docs directory.
